content: Have you ever wondered why the sun is out when we wake up, but we see stars when we go to sleep? Where does the sun go at night?
If you look outside your window right now, what color is the sky? Is it bright blue or dark black with stars? Why do you think it changes?

content.title: The Spinning Earth
content.description: Imagine a giant lamp (the sun) shining on a rotating globe (Earth). As you spin the globe, your city moves from the light into the shadow!

content: The time we have sunlight is called **Day**. The time it is dark is called **Night**. We break the day into different parts.

definition: The early part of the day when the sun rises and we wake up.
The middle part of the day when the sun is highest in the sky.
The late part of the day when the sun goes down and it starts getting dark.

content: Ask students to point to the sky and describe what it looks like right now to anchor their understanding of the current time of day.

question: When do you usually see the stars twinkling in the sky?

content: Think about your favorite game. Do you play it in the morning, afternoon, or evening? What would happen if you tried to play outside in the middle of the night?
The cycle of Day and Night is the very first way humans measured Time! Later, you will learn how watches and clocks measure exact hours and minutes.
Mini Challenge: Draw one thing you love doing in the Morning and one thing you do at Night! Share your drawing with your teacher.
Why do we go to school on some days, but stay home to play on other days? How do people know when it's a holiday?
Can you guess how many days you have to wait for the weekend to come?

content.title: The 7-Day Train
content.description: Imagine a beautiful train with 7 colourful coaches. Each coach is one day! They always come in the exact same order, round and round.

content: The train has 7 coaches: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, and Sunday. This group of 7 days is called a **Week**.

definition: A period of seven days in a row.

content: Many students think Sunday is the last day of the week, but in many calendars, Sunday is actually the first day! However, Monday is the first day of the *school* week.

question: Which day comes right after Monday?

content: If today is Wednesday, what day will it be tomorrow? Tell your parents what fun things you want to do this Sunday!
Ancient people named the days after the Sun (Sunday), Moon (Monday), and planets! In maths, you will use these 7 days to solve fun calendar puzzles.
Recite the 7 days of the week on your fingers! When you reach Sunday, give someone a high five!
How do we know when it is time to celebrate your birthday? Why is it hot sometimes and cold at other times?
Have you noticed that some months have lots of rain, while others are very cold? How many times does the moon change before your birthday comes again?

content.title: The Wheel of Months
content.description: Imagine a giant ferris wheel with 12 cabins. It takes exactly one whole year to go all the way around! As it turns, the weather changes from summer to winter.

content: There are 12 Months in a Year: January, February, March, April, May, June, July, August, September, October, November, and December!

definition: A long period of time made up of 12 months.
A part of a year. Most months have 30 or 31 days.

question: Which is the very first month of the year?

content: Which month is your birthday in? Does it usually rain during your birthday month, or is it very sunny?
In science, you will learn that these 12 months happen because the Earth travels all the way around the Sun once!
Find a calendar in your house and try to spot the name of the current month. Ask your parents to help you find your birthday month!
